summary.title: A Tree-Walk Interpreter
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build jlox, a tree-walk interpreter for the Lox language in Java, by progressing through scanning, parsing, and evaluation before adding features one at a time.
takeaways: jlox is the first of two interpreters built in the book, written in Java.
The interpreter is built front-to-back: scanning, then parsing, then evaluating code.
Language features are added one at a time, growing a simple calculator into a full scripting language.
The complete interpreter is described as under two thousand lines of Java.
Little formal theory is required, though interpreter architecture uses some uncommon design patterns.
summary.summary: This page is the opening chapter of Crafting Interpreters, introducing jlox, the first of two interpreters for the Lox language. It explains that the book keeps theory light and code simple, with the implementation under two thousand lines of Java. The interpreter is built in phases: scanning, parsing, and evaluating code, then new language features are added one at a time. The excerpt does not show code or detailed examples.
